events.reason: heart failure and blood pressure follow-up

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
HF/CAD/HTN check. Winter is slow for work, which he says his heart appreciates. Breathless on a full flight of stairs, same as summer. One pillow. No ankle swelling. No chest pain, no nitro used in the past year. Weighs himself most mornings, steady. Shoulders sore on cold mornings.
Exam: vitals as charted. JVP not elevated. Heart regular, apical systolic murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P: HFrEF, NYHA II, euvolemic. CAD s/p LAD DES, on aspirin and clopidogrel. HTN fine. Continue all meds. BMP, CBC. Back in 6 months for the AWV, sooner if weight climbs.

events.reason: neck pain and hand weakness after motor vehicle collision

conditions.label: Neuropathic pain syndrome
conditions.note: both upper extremities, after neck injury on cervical spondylosis

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth at bedtime

reports.text: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the cervical spine without contrast. Alignment maintained. No acute fracture. No marrow edema. No prevertebral soft tissue swelling. Chronic degenerative changes with disc space narrowing, disc-osteophyte complexes and facet arthropathy at multiple levels. Craniocervical junction normal.
reports.conclusion: No acute fracture. Chronic degenerative changes of the cervical spine.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED.
CC: neck pain, both hands weak after car accident.
HPI: 68-year-old man, known cervical spondylosis and coronary disease, was the driver of a pickup struck from behind while stopped at a light this afternoon. Belted. Immediate neck pain; since then both hands feel weak and clumsy and numb. Did not pass out. Legs feel normal.
Meds: aspirin, clopidogrel, metoprolol succinate, lisinopril, furosemide, atorvastatin, pantoprazole, indomethacin as needed, SL nitroglycerin as needed. NKDA.
Exam: c-collar in place on arrival. Neck range limited by pain. Grip weak bilaterally, fine finger movements slow and clumsy. Light touch and pinprick reduced in both arms, most in the hands. Biceps and brachioradialis reflexes diminished both sides; knee and ankle reflexes normal. Lower extremity strength full. No incontinence; rectal tone intact.
MRI cervical spine: no fracture, chronic degenerative changes.
Plan: spine surgery consulted; observation overnight with neuro checks.

documents.title: Spine Surgery Consultation
documents.author: spine surgery
documents.body: Asked to see for bilateral hand weakness and sensory change after a rear-end collision on a background of cervical degenerative disease. Exam as documented by ED; lower extremities intact. MRI shows no fracture and chronic degenerative change only. No instability. Recommend nonoperative care: soft collar for comfort for 2 weeks, outpatient physical therapy, neuro checks overnight. No surgical intervention indicated. Return precautions for leg weakness, gait change, bowel or bladder change.

documents.title: Observation Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Observation 3/1 to 3/2/2024.
Reason: neck injury in a rear-end collision with bilateral hand weakness and sensory change.
Course: neuro checks stable overnight. Hand strength slightly better this morning. Burning, pins-and-needles pain in both hands keeps him up. Spine surgery: nonoperative.
Discharge diagnosis: neuropathic pain syndrome of both upper extremities after neck injury, on cervical spondylosis. No fracture.
New medication: gabapentin 300 mg at bedtime.
Continue home medications unchanged. NKDA.
Orders: soft collar as needed; outpatient PT referral to be placed by PCP.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week.

orders.reason: hand weakness and neck pain after collision, cervical spondylosis

documents.title: Post-Observation Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rear-ended last Friday, overnight observation, MRI without fracture. Hands: grip is coming back slowly, still dropping screws. Burning and tingling in both hands, worst at night; gabapentin at bedtime helps him sleep. Neck sore. Legs fine, walking fine, no bladder issues.
Exam: neck tender paraspinal, rotation limited. Grip reduced bilaterally, better than the ED described. Light touch reduced in the fingertips both hands. Biceps and brachioradialis reflexes still diminished. Gait normal.
A/P: neuropathic pain in both hands after neck injury on spondylosis, improving motor. PT referral placed. Continue gabapentin 300 at bedtime for now. No driving until he can turn his head and grip the wheel well. Recheck 4 weeks.

documents.title: Physical Therapy Initial Evaluation
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
Outpatient PT evaluation. 68M, self-employed handyman, 11 days after a rear-end collision with neck pain and bilateral hand weakness and sensory change; cervical spondylosis; nonoperative per spine surgery. Goals: return to using hand tools, fasteners, driving.
Findings: cervical rotation limited and painful; grip and pinch reduced bilaterally; fine motor (coin pickup, buttoning) slowed; sensation diminished in the fingertips; gait and balance normal.
Plan: twice weekly for 8 weeks: cervical mobility, postural work, graded grip and dexterity training, home program. Cardiac precautions noted (HFrEF, CAD).

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth three times daily

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Four weeks out. PT twice a week, likes it. Grip clearly stronger, can run a screwdriver again but tires quickly. The burning in both hands persists through the day now, not just at night. Gabapentin at bedtime tolerated, no fogginess.
Exam: grip improved bilaterally. Fingertip light touch still reduced. Neck rotation better.
A/P: neuropathic pain syndrome, hands; motor recovering. Gabapentin increased to 300 mg three times daily. Kidney function normal on last labs. Caution re drowsiness on ladders. Continue PT. Back to driving short trips is reasonable now.

documents.title: Physical Therapy Discharge Summary
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body: Discharged from PT after 15 visits (one missed). Cervical rotation now functional both directions. Grip and pinch close to expected for age and work; dexterity tasks within normal time. Residual intermittent burning in the fingertips, managed by his physician. Independent with home exercise program.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm. Anterior Q waves with persistent ST elevation, unchanged from prior tracings.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Cardiology Annual Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Letter to PCP. Seen for yearly review of CAD (proximal LAD DES 1/2023), ischemic cardiomyopathy with anterior aneurysm and HFrEF. No angina. Stable class II symptoms. Car accident in March with hand symptoms, now on gabapentin. ECG unchanged. Euvolemic on exam.
Medications: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, furosemide 40, atorvastatin 40, pantoprazole 40, gabapentin 300 TID, indomethacin as needed, NTG SL as needed. NKDA.
Plan: continue current therapy including dual antiplatelet therapy. Return in one year.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, age 69. Grip back to where it was before the accident since about June, back to small carpentry jobs. Fingertip burning still there most days but milder on gabapentin 300 TID. Neck stiff as always. Heart: stairs with mild breathlessness, unchanged. Saw cardiology in June, no changes.
No falls. PHQ-2 negative. Lives alone, independent.
Exam: vitals as charted. Grip strong and symmetric. Fingertip light touch mildly reduced. Heart regular, apical murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.
Plan: CMP, lipids, CBC. Fall vaccines: flu, COVID, and RSV this year given his heart failure. LDCT November.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Three vaccines today per PCP: high-dose flu L deltoid, RSV (Abrysvo) R deltoid, 2024-25 Moderna COVID L deltoid lower site. Pressure held on each (on DAPT). Waited 15 minutes, no reaction. Told him a sore arm tomorrow would not be surprising.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Low-dose noncontrast CT of the chest compared with 11/2023. No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or pleural effusion. Airways patent.

documents.title: LDCT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lung-RADS 1 again. Sent to portal.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: No-show for 7:30 follow-up. Reached him at 9:05: forgot, was on a job in Hartland plowing out a client's walkway. Rebooked for 1/14. Reminded about texting the office if anything changes with breathing or weight.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rebooked from December. Doing OK. Stairs with some breathlessness, about the same. Sleeping flat on one pillow. No swelling. Home weights steady. Hand burning a 3 out of 10 most days.
Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular, apical systolic murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P: HFrEF stable. CAD, no angina. Neuropathic hand pain controlled on gabapentin. BMP. Continue meds; see in spring.

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Bilateral perihilar airspace opacities in a pattern of pulmonary edema. No pneumothorax.
Dilated LV with anterior aneurysm, unchanged in appearance. LVEF 30%. Moderate functional mitral regurgitation. RV normal size. No pericardial effusion.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED.
69-year-old man with ischemic cardiomyopathy, HFrEF and anterior LV aneurysm after an old MI. For two weeks breathlessness has crept up: a flight of stairs or a short walk now stops him. Wakes at night gasping and has gone to three pillows. No chest pain, fever or recent illness.
Vitals: T 36.9, BP 102/66, HR 108, RR 24, SpO2 89% on room air.
Exam: mildly distressed, using accessory muscles. Late inspiratory crackles at both bases, no wheeze. S3 gallop. Mild pitting edema both legs.
CXR: bilateral perihilar opacities, pulmonary edema. NT-proBNP 4850. Troponin not elevated.
Plan: oxygen, IV furosemide, admit to the cardiac unit. NKDA.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Admitted 2/26/2025, discharged 3/3/2025.
Diagnosis: acute decompensated heart failure, HFrEF, ischemic cardiomyopathy with anterior LV aneurysm.
Course: hypoxic with pulmonary edema on arrival. A pulmonary artery catheter was placed in the cardiac unit on the first night to guide therapy given soft blood pressure; wedge pressure elevated at 27 mmHg. IV furosemide with good response, oxygen weaned by day 3, catheter removed day 3. Echo: LVEF 30%, aneurysm unchanged, moderate functional MR. Troponin not elevated, no ischemic trigger found. Weight down 5 kg at discharge. Renal function stable.
Discharge medications (unchanged from home): aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, furosemide 40 daily, atorvastatin 40, pantoprazole 40, gabapentin 300 TID, indomethacin as needed, NTG SL as needed.
NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week, cardiology 2-3 weeks. Daily weights, 2 g sodium diet, fluid around 2 L.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First heart failure admission, 2/26 to 3/3, pulmonary edema, diuresed, PA catheter, EF now 30%. Home 3 days. Breathing much better, back to one pillow, can do the porch steps. Weighing daily, holding at discharge weight. Discharge meds reviewed line by line with his pill box: unchanged from before.
Exam: vitals as charted. No JVD. Heart regular, apical systolic murmur, no gallop today. Faint crackles right base. Trace ankle edema.
A/P: HFrEF after decompensation, near dry weight. Continue furosemide 40 daily; extra dose only on instruction. Low-salt diet reviewed. BMP today. Cardiology 3/20.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Seen after his first heart failure hospitalization (late February). Now euvolemic, class II, weight stable at home. LVEF 30% on the inpatient echo with the known anterior aneurysm.
Medications unchanged: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, furosemide 40, atorvastatin 40, pantoprazole 40, gabapentin, indomethacin as needed, NTG SL as needed. NKDA.
Plan: continue current regimen. Sodium and fluid guidance reinforced. Return in 6 months.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, 70 last month. Since the February admission he has kept to light jobs. Stairs with mild breathlessness. One pillow. Weights steady. Hands burn mildly; gabapentin continues. Shoulders and elbows ache after work.
Mood screen PHQ-9 4. No falls. Lives alone; brother nearby.
Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular, murmur unchanged. Lungs clear. No edema.
Plan: CMP, lipids, CBC. Flu and COVID in the fall. LDCT in November. Colonoscopy due 2027. Cardiology in September.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED.
70M with HFrEF and an anterior LV aneurysm from a prior anterior MI years ago, admitted here in February for decompensated heart failure. Over the last several days, breathlessness has steadily worsened; he wakes up gasping and sleeps propped up on several pillows. Appetite down, legs a little swollen. No chest pain, cough or fever.
Exam: tired, short of breath at rest. S3. Crackles at both bases, no wheeze. JVP elevated. Peripheral pulses weak.
CXR: increased vascular markings, small bilateral effusions. NT-proBNP 6120, troponin not elevated.
Impression: acute pulmonary edema from left heart failure.
Plan: IV diuresis, admit to the cardiac unit; pulmonary artery catheter for hemodynamic monitoring. NKDA.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Admitted 9/4/2025, discharged 9/9/2025.
Diagnosis: acute pulmonary edema due to left heart failure; HFrEF (LVEF 30% 2/2025), ischemic cardiomyopathy with anterior aneurysm.
Course: pulmonary artery catheter placed in the cardiac unit for hemodynamic monitoring; PCWP 25 mmHg on placement. IV furosemide, brisk diuresis, catheter out on day 2, off oxygen day 3. Renal function stable. Weight down about 4 kg.
Discharge medications unchanged from home: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, furosemide 40, atorvastatin 40, pantoprazole 40, gabapentin 300 TID, indomethacin 25 as needed, NTG SL as needed.
NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within a week, cardiology next month.

conditions.label: Acute pulmonary edema due to left heart failure

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Second HF admission this year, 9/4 to 9/9, acute pulmonary edema, PA catheter, IV diuresis. Discharged on the same regimen. Feels much better; one pillow again; walked the driveway twice yesterday. Daily weights at discharge weight.
Exam: vitals as charted. No JVD. Heart regular, apical murmur, no S3 today. Lungs clear. Trace edema.
A/P: pulmonary edema resolved; HFrEF back to dry weight. Low-sodium cooking reviewed again; he will keep a weight log on the fridge. BMP today. Cardiology in October. Flu and COVID at that time too.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu and 2025-26 COVID given. Pressure held, no bleeding. Weight log reviewed at the door: stable.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body: Follow-up after September admission for pulmonary edema. Euvolemic and stable since. Regimen continued without change: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, furosemide 40, atorvastatin 40, pantoprazole 40. NKDA. Return in 4 to 6 months.

documents.author: patient
documents.body: Can you send refills for the metoprolol, furosemide and gabapentin so I'm not scrambling at the end of the month. Also the stomach pill. Weight's holding.
